posts.headline: Look up any nursing home before you visit
posts.subhead: Four checks that take under ten minutes.
changes: Check the 1-to-5 star rating: it combines health inspections, staffing, and quality measures in one score.
Read the last three years of health inspection reports to see citations, what was wrong, and whether it was fixed.
Check staffing: look for nurse hours per resident per day and staff turnover — more hours, less turnover is better.
Look for any Medicare penalties — a fine or denied payment — listed on the facility's Care Compare page.
posts.verdict_text: A quick Care Compare search before you visit can reveal inspection citations, low staffing, or Medicare penalties that a tour alone will not show.
actions: Search any NJ nursing home free at medicare.gov/care-compare
Call NJ Long-Term Care Ombudsman: 1-877-582-6995 (all NJ counties)
File a care complaint with NJ Dept. of Health: 1-800-792-9770
posts.caption_rendered:
BEFORE YOU CHOOSE

Before you tour a nursing home in Bergen, Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, or Warren County, spend a few minutes on Care Compare. The free federal tool shows you each facility's star rating across three areas: health inspections, staffing levels, and quality measures. You can read the actual inspection reports from the past three years, see how many nurse hours per day each resident receives on average, check staff turnover rates, and find out whether Medicare has ever fined or penalized the facility. None of that shows up on a lobby tour. Use what you find online to form sharper questions when you walk in the door. Source: Medicare.gov Care Compare.
